selector_distortion_theorem.setup: At each reporting time t let Tj=Ej_t(mu0) be the two target evidences used by the exact nine-split minimax selector, and Vj=Ej_t(theta_j) be valid e-processes at the two fixed true parameters. The selected split is alpha1=i*delta/10, alpha2=(10-i)*delta/10, i=1,...,9.
selector_distortion_theorem.selection_geometry: If split i is selected, T1/T2 lies in [(9-i)/i,(10-i)/(i-1)] with the natural 0/infinity endpoint conventions.
selector_distortion_theorem.distortion_condition: Let qj=Tj/Vj. If 1/K <= q2/q1 <= K for every reporting time, then selected-pair numerical miscoverage is anytime-bounded by 2*delta/c(K), where c(K)=min_i [10/i * (1+(i-1)/((10-i)K))]. The channel-2 branch is the same expression after i -> 10-i.
proof: If channel 1 miscovers under split i, V1>=10/(i*delta). Selection geometry and q2/q1<=K imply V1/V2<=((10-i)/(i-1))*K, hence V1+V2 >= [10/(i*delta)]*[1+(i-1)/((10-i)K)].
The channel-2 case is symmetric. Therefore any selected-pair miscoverage implies V1+V2>=c(K)/delta.
Because (V1+V2)/2 is an e-process under the joint true parameters, Ville gives P(any selected-pair miscoverage)<=2*delta/c(K). Channel independence is not required.
selector_distortion_theorem.key_corollary: K<=5 implies c(K)>=2, so the same-history selected pair has anytime numerical miscoverage probability <=delta. This is a sufficient condition, not a generic post-selection theorem.

v3_component_ratio_certificate.identity: For each channel and lambda component, Ej_lambda(mu0)/Ej_lambda(theta)=d_lambda(theta)/d_lambda(mu0); the score-dependent numerator cancels. Because the production V3 is a positive mixture of these components, qj=Ej(mu0)/Ej(theta) is a data-dependent convex combination of the component ratios.
v3_component_ratio_certificate.score_independent_bounds: Define Lj=min_lambda d_j,lambda(theta_j)/d_j,lambda(mu0) and Uj=max_lambda of the same ratio. Then qj lies in [Lj,Uj] pathwise, and K=max(U2/L1,U1/L2) is a sufficient distortion bound based only on the predictable weight history and the candidate true parameters.
v3_component_ratio_certificate.importance: This is stronger than monotonicity alone: it links the target evidence used for selection to the true-parameter evidence used for numerical coverage without assuming the target e-values themselves are valid at the off-target truth.

numerical_scope_audit.common_mean_family: Both channels observe the same Bernoulli conditional mean theta. Equal-process weights are all 1; planned-exposure weights alternate .25,1 starting with .25; mu0=.05; production V3 lambdas are used.

prefix_grid_t_1_to_40_theta_0_to_0_05.interpretation: Finite-grid numerical evidence is consistent with the K<=5 sufficient condition throughout these prefixes; this is not a continuum proof.

numerical_scope_audit.interpretation: The sufficient condition can hold for short/near-target histories and fail badly for longer/far-off-target histories. Same-history reuse therefore needs an explicit distortion-domain guard or a fresh-confirm/fixed-alpha fallback; history length alone is not a certificate.

off_target_optional_stress.model: Independent Bernoulli blocks with predictable alternating weights .25,1; same-history exact nine-split minimax selector recomputed through horizon 300; numerical crossing checked against each channel's running true weighted mean. 100000 trajectories per condition.
off_target_optional_stress.interpretation: These V3-shaped off-target stresses exceed the earlier 2.7778% target-null theorem bound in some cases, confirming that target-null safety must not be transplanted off target. They remained below 5% in these tested conditions, but Monte Carlo is negative stress evidence only and does not establish general coverage.

public_context.title: Post-selection inference for e-value based confidence intervals
public_context.authors: Ziyu Xu, Ruodu Wang, Aaditya Ramdas
public_context.relevance: Provides a generic e-CI post-selection/FCR route under arbitrary selection/dependence; it is a portable fallback context, distinct from the selector-specific K-distortion theorem derived here.

scope_guards: The theorem requires V1_t=E1_t(theta1) and V2_t=E2_t(theta2) to be valid e-processes at fixed true parameters and requires the K distortion bound uniformly over all reporting times used for the anytime claim.
For running-average conditional-mean targets that change with t, do not substitute the moving true mean into this fixed-parameter theorem without a separate domination argument.

K depends on the true parameters. A deployable guard over an unknown parameter requires a predeclared parameter domain and a uniform worst-case K bound over that domain and allowed predictable weight histories; post-hoc observed K at a guessed theta is not a coverage certificate.
The finite theta-grid prefix audit and the 100000-path stresses are numerical evidence, not analytic coverage proofs.
The K<=5 result is specific to the exact nine-split minimax selector geometry; arbitrary same-history alpha selectors remain unsafe without a separate correction.
Fresh-confirm remains the portable no-selection-penalty reporting route when the distortion-domain condition cannot be certified.
